I need to be careful here: the trolley scenario has the train heading toward one worker, and pulling the lever diverts it onto five, so pulling the lever actually kills more people, not fewer. Several answers seem to misread this, claiming pulling the lever minimizes harm, so I want to flag that error. I'm categorizing responses into consistent-procedure versus consequence-reasoning types to note what each actually states.

Going through the remaining answers: some frame it as following the same process regardless of personal cost or who's on the track, weighing five against one; another touches on responsibility for a death but ultimately denies rather than affirms responsibility, so I'm marking it as rule-justification rather than a responsibility acknowledgment; the rest continue the same pattern of choosing the lower-toll option consistently.
